findings.title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and never normalizes addresses
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the exact string supplied, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator downcases/strips the address (nor is there normalization when a BlockedEmail record is created). PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so a blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is bypassed by registering as `Bad@Spam.com`, `BAD@spam.com`, etc., defeating the block list this PR introduces. Normalize (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and in should_block?/the validator lookup.

findings.title: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write save during validation, double-counting and losing concurrent updates
findings.body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator during User validation, yet it mutates and saves the BlockedEmail record (`match_count += 1; last_match_at = ...; record.save`). Validation is not a single occurrence: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which re-validates, so one signup attempt increments match_count at least twice, and any other `valid?` check also permanently increments it even if the user is never saved. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts reading the same match_count overwrite each other and lose counts. Use an atomic increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with a separate last_match_at update) and avoid counting purely on validation, or at minimum make the update atomic.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and shared across instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares a mutable array as a class/prototype property. Ember shares prototype object/array values across instances until reassigned, and createAccount mutates it in place with `pushObject(result.values.email)` rather than setting a new array. Rejected addresses can therefore leak/persist across controller instances and account-creation attempts instead of starting empty per instance. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in init/create) rather than as a shared prototype array.
